     Unlike the two plain-pair reports beside it, this comparison is NOT bitwise
     identical, and that is the finding. -->

**Verdict: NOT equivalent — `-nocheckpoint` changes what `adjViscBoost` does.**
The adjViscBoost build was given the default `-nocheckpoint` list on
2026-09-02 and revalidated against run 31025 (the same build without the
list, 30 d from rest, live `input_tap/data`). `fc` and all 441 `%MON` lines
are byte-identical (the forward trajectory is untouched, as always), but every
`ADJ*` dump and every real `adxx_*` gradient differ at order one (RMS ratio
0.3–0.9, max ratio up to 1.4), while the plain pair (31054 vs 31052, 31055 vs
31039) is bitwise identical under the same list. Mechanism: in joint
(checkpointed) mode Tapenade re-runs each routine's primal inside the backward
sweep, *after* the mode-switch adjoint (`TAP_INADMODE_SET_B` in the builds
compared, `AUTODIFF_INADMODE_SET_B` since 2026-09-02) has switched the viscosities to the
`inAd*` values, so the boost reaches every recomputed intermediate (the
per-level viscosity fields of `mom_calc_visc`, the tendencies of `timestep`,
…); in split mode those intermediates were taped during the forward sweep at
the *forward* viscosities, so the boost reaches only what the `_BWD` code
reads live. The two are different regularisations, and only the joint-mode
one is what the ASTE/TAF-style boost was designed as and what 31025 validated.
Consequence: `build_tapAdj_adjViscBoost.sh` does **not** carry the list (it
was reverted the same day, run token `tapAdj_ckpAll_adjViscBoost`); 31056 stays
on scratch as the record of the split-mode variant. Its
`comparison_vs_…_run31025.txt` from `tools/compare_adj_runs.sh` gives the same
verdict (74 of 196 sensitivity files differ; the packed control gradient
`ecco_cost_MIT_CE_000.opt0000` differs accordingly).
